intro: Estimate your body fat percentage using the US Navy circumference method. No expensive equipment needed — just a measuring tape.

ranges.title: Body Fat Categories (American Council on Exercise)

formula.title: US Navy Method Formula
formula.explanation: The US Navy method uses circumference measurements to estimate body density, which is then converted to body fat percentage using the Siri equation.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: How accurate is the US Navy body fat method?
faq.a1: The US Navy method has an error margin of approximately ±3–4% compared to DEXA scans. It is more accurate than BMI for estimating body composition but less precise than laboratory methods.
faq.q2: Where should I measure my waist?
faq.a2: Measure your waist at the level of the navel (belly button) for this method. Keep the tape parallel to the floor and do not suck in your stomach.
faq.q3: What is a healthy body fat percentage?
faq.a3: Acceptable ranges are roughly 18–24% for men and 25–31% for women. Athletes typically fall in the 6–17% (men) and 14–24% (women) range.
faq.q4: Can I reduce body fat without losing muscle?
faq.a4: Yes. A moderate calorie deficit combined with sufficient protein intake (1.6–2.2 g/kg) and resistance training preserves lean mass while reducing fat mass.
faq.q5: Why is my body fat different from my BMI category?
faq.a5: BMI measures weight relative to height and does not account for body composition. Muscular individuals may have a high BMI but low body fat, while sedentary people may have normal BMI but high body fat.
